note: Every declared runtime operation, with the evidence that does and does not exist for it. An operation is SUPPORTED only when a committed test drives it to a validated success AND a validated refusal across its public transport boundary — a started MCP host over stdio, a real HTTP /tool request with bridge auth, or the gateway serving boundary. In-process callability (the coverage smoke matrix) and a console/gateway binding are recorded as facts but do not confer support: an in-process Python call does not cross the transport. No such public-transport success+refusal evidence exists yet, so every operation is deferred pending separately scoped transport work. Regenerate, do not hand-edit. Partial success-only evidence is catalogued in docs/evidence/transport-evidence-appendix.md.
status_rule: supported iff a committed test crosses the public transport (MCP host / HTTP /tool / gateway serving) for BOTH success and refusal, recorded in transport_proven; the channel names that transport. Otherwise deferred. In-process coverage and surface bindings never confer support.

status_vocabulary.ui-supported: success+refusal proven across a real HTTP /tool request
status_vocabulary.gateway-supported: success+refusal proven across the gateway serving boundary
status_vocabulary.mcp-supported: success+refusal proven across a started MCP host over stdio
status_vocabulary.experimental: demo-only surface, not a supported capability
status_vocabulary.deferred: no public-transport success+refusal evidence (may still be surfaced or in-process callable)

operations.basis: deferred: no committed test crosses this operation's public transport (MCP host / HTTP /tool / gateway serving) for success and refusal. Recorded evidence — console binding present; source-grep route present. Promotion is separately scoped transport work.
HTTP /tool success and fail-closed session-token refusal are exercised against the live server; the About render gate drives server_info through that bridge.
